body.body:
Though it was noted that making `UNINITIALIZED_VALUE` just an instance of `Any` may complicate debugging, because instead of the name of the class `UNINITIALIZED_VALUE@5305068a` you'll get something like `java.lang.Object@5305068a` when evaluating/watching over lazy instance fields.

The proposed solution is to introduce internal enum for all such constant-like objects in the standard library.

@ilya-g Could as well be just a `String` wrapper that prints its value in `toString()`, which could be reused in all parts of the stdlib. Cleaner than the enum IMO because the purpose of each object stays where it's used, and not in a god-like place.
Historically `UNINITIALIZED_VALUE` was declared as object because Kotlin/JS didn't support instantiation of `Any()`. Now this limitation is gone, so we can rewrite it this way.
